title: WW3 DEBATE: “We’re On the Brink of Global Collapse”
summary: A 2026 podcast debate among three analysts on the Iran war, US decline, China and Taiwan, and whether today's regional wars will become a world war.

assertions.quote: I don't see a global conflict coming. Many regional conflicts are coming because the global system is restructuring itself.

verdicts.note: Conflict data show regional wars multiplying while forecasters keep a direct great-power war well below even odds in any given year, though this is a forecast.

PRIO: today's interstate conflicts are border disputes, invasions and a Middle East regional escalation that could become a larger regional war, which fits the claim for now but says nothing of the future.

assertions.quote: The Russian army could not take Ukraine after five years. This is not a military threat.

verdicts.note: Russia's conventional forces are far weaker than NATO's combined, but it could mount a limited attack on a frontline state and holds a large nuclear arsenal.

DDIS says Ukraine ties up most Russian resources now, but Russia's reform and rearmament aim to make it able to win a war against NATO on its western borders, with readiness for a regional war within about two years of the Ukraine war ending.
US intelligence calls Russia's robust conventional and nuclear forces an enduring threat to US allies, with ground forces grown and air and naval forces intact.

assertions.quote: continue to support NATO expansion and and uh um make Ukraine a much much stronger country even after Putin uh takes Crimea in 2014

verdicts.note: NATO's 2008 promise to Ukraine was one grievance Moscow cited, but most historians weigh Russian imperial aims and Ukraine's turn to the EU at least as heavily, so a single provoking cause overstates it.

assertions.quote: it is very likely that all the world powers are brought are brought in. China is brought into the war.

verdicts.note: The 2025 and 2026 rounds stayed regional and Russia and China kept out, so escalation to great-power war is possible but unlikely.

assertions.quote: I don't think we're heading to a war with China if we're smart

verdicts.note: Forecasters put a US-China war in the coming years at low odds, and the two governments were negotiating trade and summit deals through 2025 and 2026.
Metaculus's 629 forecasters put a US-China war (1,000 battle deaths in a year) at 8.7% before 2035; linked questions put it at 25% before 2050 and 0.5% by 2027.
FRI's median expert put 500+ militarized deaths between China and the US by 2030 at 10% (superforecasters 6%).

70% of surveyed strategists expect China to try to take Taiwan by force within a decade (up from 50% two years earlier) and over 40% envision a great-power world war: a rising expectation, short of war being the most likely outcome.
DDIS sees a lasting rivalry with both sides building up for 'a potential military confrontation that neither side wants', which is preparation, not a predicted war.
Eurasia Group calls imminent US-China conflict a 'red herring' for 2026, not even a top risk.

Hanania argues that Allison's 12-of-16 record, the main evidence for a coming US-China war, has fatal flaws (unclear definitions, omitted variables, selection bias), and that the post-1950 record of power shifts with no war gives a more optimistic view. This is an argument against the evidence, not a forecast of its own.

assertions.quote: It is the number one trading partner and it is the only military threat to China. Therefore, accommodation is rational for China

verdicts.note: SIPRI says the assumption that trade interdependence would generate peace 'has given way to the increasing weaponization of trade', which weakens the pacifying mechanism without measuring its effect on war risk.

assertions.quote: if China plays its cards right, Taiwan is going to fall right into China's lap

verdicts.note: Polls in Taiwan show support for unification in single digits and a rising Taiwanese identity, so peaceful absorption looks unlikely on current trends.

assertions.quote: I don't see any scenario where nuclear weapons are used even tactically

verdicts.note: Forecasters put nuclear use in any given year at a few percent at most, though the risk is not zero.
Metaculus forecasters put any non-test nuclear detonation anywhere at 0.5% before 2027, 2.4% before 2028 and 5.1% before 2030.
78% of the surveyed strategists predict no nuclear use in the next ten years (up from 52% a year earlier); 15% expect Russian use.
US intelligence judges Russia will probably keep abiding by the norm against large-scale nuclear use unless the Ukraine war shifts significantly, so non-use is likely but conditional.

assertions.quote: What I'm saying is we're moving to a more warprone world.

verdicts.note: Conflict datasets show state-based conflicts at their highest since the Second World War and US dominance has eroded, but most of the new fighting is not between great powers.
Kroenig links the world's peak safety to the US unipolar moment and says respondents expect diminishing US leadership to accelerate the decline; an expert view rather than measured war-proneness.
DDIS links a shift in the balance of power away from US dominance to states increasingly asserting their will by economic and military power and rising distrust, without measuring war-proneness.

UCDP: more states fighting interstate conflicts or arming rebels challenge the US-led order, and the record 2025 count lends credence to talk of the end of Pax Americana; this is a correlation, not a tested cause.

The WEF report says that as a unipolar world becomes multipolar and multilateral constraints weaken, a less predictable and more militarized environment carries a heightened risk of conflicts, with weaker countries most exposed. This is expert judgement from a perception survey, not a measured trend in great-power war.

assertions.quote: in this emerging anarchy you will see greater uh incentives for nuclear proliferation

verdicts.note: Public debate about national bombs has grown in Poland, South Korea and elsewhere, but no ally has started a weapons programme.

Most respondents expect new nuclear states within a decade (South Korea 47% and Japan 37% of them), which Woolf links to doubts about US extended deterrence: an expectation and an interpretation, not observed proliferation.
The Bulletin reports that doubts about US extended deterrence have led European states to debate a Euro-deterrent or nuclear latency, and South Korea and Japan to hold similar debates.
US intelligence says countries without WMD may pursue them partly because of greater doubts about existing security agreements, without naming US allies seeking nuclear weapons.

assertions.quote: it creates the opportunity for Iran to really uh close and try to shut down Hormuz
even heavy economic pressure alone, I mean alone without other military force has never won a major war

verdicts.note: Studies of blockades and sanctions find they rarely force a major power to give in without military defeat, though the answer depends on how strictly 'alone' is read.
